html:
Newgrange is a huge passage tomb in the Boyne valley in Ireland, built about 3200 BCE by Neolithic farmers. It is older than Stonehenge and the pyramids of Giza.

A round mound of earth and stone, about 85 metres across, covers a long passage leading to a cross-shaped chamber. Above the entrance is a roof-box: at sunrise on the days around the winter solstice a beam of light runs down the passage and lights the chamber floor. Large kerbstones around the mound are carved with spirals.

With nearby Knowth and Dowth it forms Brú na Bóinne, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. In Irish myth it was the home of the gods, the Tuatha Dé Danann. It shows that farming communities in Ireland could organise great works long before the Celts, at about the time Malta's temples were built.
sum: Newgrange is a huge passage tomb in the Boyne valley in Ireland, built about 3200 BCE by Neolithic farmers. It is older than Stonehenge and the pyramids of Giza.
